taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find when 11:59 PM PT on Friday, October 30, 2026 is in Madrid time.

**Step 1: Identify the deadline.**
Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT.

**Step 2: Determine PT offset.**
PT = Pacific Time. In late October, the US clocks fall back on the first Sunday of November. October 30, 2026 is still before that, so PT is still PDT (UTC−7).

**Step 3: Determine Madrid time offset.**
Spain (Madrid) changes clocks on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So by October 30, Spain is on CET (UTC+1).

**Step 4: Convert.**
- Deadline: October 30, 2026 at 23:59 PDT = October 31, 2026 at 06:59 UTC
- Madrid (UTC+1): October 31, 2026 at 07:59

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Deadline:** Monday, November 2, 2026, at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time.

Los Angeles uses Pacific Time. In November 2026, I need to check DST status:
- US DST ends the first Sunday of November → November 1, 2026.
- So on November 2, 2026, Los Angeles is on **PST (UTC−8)**.

Madrid in November 2026:
- Europe DST ends the last Sunday of October → October 25, 2026.
- So on November 2, 2026, Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

**Time difference:** Madrid is UTC+1, Los Angeles is UTC−8 → Madrid is **9 hours ahead**.

10:00 AM Los Angeles PST = 10:00 + 9:00 = **19:00 Madrid time**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid time in late October 2026: Spain switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25.

The clocks go back at 3:00 AM CEST → 2:00 AM CET on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Start: Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time (CEST, UTC+2)
Duration: 48 hours

Counting 48 hours from Saturday Oct 24 18:00:
- +24h = Sunday, Oct 25, 18:00 (but clocks fell back at 3:00 AM, so by 18:00 on Sunday we're in CET)
- +48h = Monday, Oct 26, 18:00 Madrid local time (CET)

Since the clocks fell back during the hackathon, the wall-clock time adds an extra hour, but the problem states the hackathon lasts **exactly 48 hours** — meaning 48 real hours from 18:00 on Oct 24.

18:00 CEST = 16:00 UTC. 
16:00 UTC + 48h = 16:00 UTC on Oct 26. 
Oct 26 is in CET (UTC+1), so local time = 17:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Start:** October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (Pacific Time)

**72 hours later:** October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT

**PT to Madrid time conversion:**

PT = UTC−7 (PDT, since October 26 is still before the US fall back on November 1, 2026)

Madrid in late October: Spain changes clocks on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So by October 26, Spain is already on CET (UTC+1).

- October 26: Spain = UTC+1, PT = UTC−7 → Madrid is **+8 hours** ahead of PT
- October 29: Same situation (Spain already fell back, US hasn't yet) → Madrid is still **+8 hours** ahead of PT

**Deadline in Madrid time:**
October 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT + 8 hours = October 29, 2026 at **18:00**

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

## Reasoning

**Submissions close:** October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET

**ET in late October:** The US falls back from EDT (UTC-4) to EST (UTC-5) on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's November 1. So on October 31, ET is still **EDT = UTC-4**.

**Convert to UTC:** 11:59 PM EDT = 23:59 + 4h = **November 1, 2026 at 03:59 UTC**

**Add 36 hours:** November 1, 03:59 UTC + 36 hours = **November 2, 2026 at 15:59 UTC**

**Madrid local time in November:** Spain switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So by November 2, Madrid is on **CET = UTC+1**.

**Convert to Madrid time:** 15:59 UTC + 1h = **16:59 local time on November 2, 2026**

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59
